title: Affine ordinary tensor homology coordinates with one normalized comparison per basic inclusion
statement: Let Y be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], M and N quasi-coherent O_Y-modules [pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and, for every affine open U, let MA_U and NA_U be modules over A_U=Gamma(Y,U), with specified A_U-linear equivalences sM_U:MA_U -> Gamma(U,M) and sN_U:NA_U -> Gamma(U,N). Let P_U be a nonnegative projective resolution of MA_U. Let K be an arbitrary, possibly unbounded, K-flat complex [def-pc-kflat-complex] of O_Y-modules, with a quasi-isomorphism q:K -> M[0] [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules], and let n be a natural number. Put Q=H^{-n}(Tot(K tensor N[0])) [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. There is a family of A_U-linear equivalences c_U:H_n(P_U tensor NA_U) -> Gamma(U,Q) such that for every basic inclusion V subset U, with restriction phi:A_U -> A_V, there exist a phi-semilinear coefficient map b:NA_U -> NA_V, a chain map a:P_U -> Res_phi(P_V), and a chain map k:(P_U tensor NA_U) -> Res_phi(P_V tensor NA_V), satisfying all four conditions: sM_V(pi_V(a_0 x))=res_M(sM_U(pi_U x)); sN_V(b y)=res_N(sN_U y); k_j(x tensor y)=a_j(x) tensor b(y) for every j,x,y; and res_Q(c_U x)=c_V(e(H_n(k)(x))) for every homology class x, where e is the canonical exact restriction-of-scalars homology isomorphism. The maps b,a,k are existential witnesses for each inclusion; the statement does not assert the section square for every augmented comparison.

proof.text: For each affine U, use the tilde-Gamma adjunction and the supplied section equivalences sM_U and sN_U to identify the associated sheaves of MA_U and NA_U with M restricted to U and N restricted to U. Normalize these isomorphisms by the actual section equations toOpen(m) maps to sM_U(m), and analogously for N. The affine unit and quasi-coherent counit are isomorphisms. Sheafify P_U and its augmentation and place chain degree j in cochain degree -j; exact associated sheaf preserves the augmentation quasi-isomorphism.

The terms of P_U are projective, hence flat, and its cochain extension is bounded above, so it is K-flat by the bounded-flat criterion. Associated sheaf preserves K-flatness. The supplied K remains K-flat after restricting to U. Choose a K-flat resolution of the second coefficient N restricted to U. The two tensor zigzags through this common resolution compare the ordinary tensors computed using K restricted to U and the sheafified P_U; each leg is a quasi-isomorphism by K-flat tensor invariance. Use the open tensor-homology comparison to identify their homology.

Identify the sheafified tensor complex with the associated sheaf of P_U tensor NA_U using the affine chart total-tensor isomorphism. Apply the natural exact tilde homology comparison, the degree -n cochain-extension identification with chain homology in degree n, and the affine sections unit. Compose with the previous tensor-homology comparison to obtain c_U, with the prescribed coefficient normalization.

For a basic inclusion V subset U, define b using restriction of N conjugated by sN_U and sN_V. Define the analogous semilinear map on MA by restriction of M conjugated by sM. Restrict P_V along phi; exact restriction of scalars keeps its augmentation exact. Projectivity of each P_U term lifts the induced augmentation map successively through these exact differentials, giving a. The degree-zero lift has the stated sM augmentation equation. Define k on pure tensors by a_j(x) tensor b(y); the balancing relation, the chain-map equation for a and additivity give the tensor chain map and its displayed formula. These are constructions inside the existence proof, not data taken from an unproved existence theorem in a definition.

Restrict both chart tensor zigzags to V and compare them using a common K-flat resolution of the second coefficient. The normalized sM augmentation equation identifies the sheafification of a with restriction of M after augmentation, and the normalized sN equation does the same for b and N. The pure tensor formula identifies k with their tensor comparison. Functoriality of tensor and of the common-resolution zigzag gives the commuting comparison squares. Apply homology and cancel their invertible legs. Naturality of the affine chart total-tensor isomorphism, exact tilde homology and the affine sections unit gives res_Q(c_U x)=c_V(e(H_n(k)(x))). This is the geometric naturality obligation for the one constructed comparison; independence from every other comparison is deliberately left to the parent coordinate theorem. No boundedness of K, flatness of phi, positive-degree assumption, or nonzero ring or module assumption is used.
